result:
Here's a draft. I worded it as "copy complete" rather than "migration complete" because the only evidence so far is the script's own `in==out` line. Deleting the old bucket is hard to reverse, so I'd confirm a few things first and fill in the bracketed parts before posting.

**Draft**

> **Customer attachments: S3 migration copy complete**
>
> The copy of customer attachments from `[old-bucket]` to `[new-bucket]` has finished: 48,213 objects copied, 0 errors.
>
> Independent verification: `[object count and total size match on both buckets via aws s3 ls --recursive --summarize / checksum spot-check of N objects / other]`
>
> Current state:
> - `[App/services now read and write to new-bucket as of date]`
> - `[No writes to old-bucket since date/time, confirmed via access logs]`
>
> Plan: if nothing turns up this week, we'll delete `[old-bucket]` on **[date]**. If you see missing or broken attachments, reply here before then.
>
> Owner for the deletion: `[name]`

**Why I'd check before posting**

- **The script graded its own work.** `in==out` is the copier's self-report. A separate count and size comparison (or ETag/checksum sample) from the S3 side is a stronger check and takes a couple of minutes.
- **Objects added after the copy started.** If anything was still writing to the old bucket, those objects won't be in the 48,213. The note should say when writes moved to the new bucket.
- **Versions and delete markers.** If the old bucket is versioned, confirm whether the script copied only current versions and whether that's acceptable.
- **References to the old bucket.** Check for hardcoded bucket names or presigned URLs, as well as CDN origins, IAM policies, and lifecycle or replication rules.
- **The one-week window.** It is only useful if someone is actually watching for breakage, so name an owner.

If you tell me the bucket names, dates, and what verification you ran, I can fill in the placeholders and tighten the note.
